byOutcome.paired: We tried two loops on an Emberford basket today. I asked the person holding it which side would help. That is the thing I forgot to do with our case. I used to think a hand held out was a very small tool.
byOutcome.mended: I taught an Emberford trader the stitch we used on the case. He wanted to put my name on a card at his stall. I asked him to put the stitch there. I’ll tell my own story when I have words for it.

byOutcome.public: I’ve split a receipt on the road again. One line is public, and the receiver can still ask at the desk about where it came from. It adds four breaths to my handover. I timed it.
byOutcome.desk: I wrote the hours on the outside of my next folder. A runner can take them to someone who has a record to show. That person can choose when to come and who sees their name.
byOutcome.leave: I kept a blank receiving line on the next form. The supervisor frowned until someone came back with a docket we had missed. The blank finally had a job to do.

byOutcome.rail: The low mark on the rail case stayed dry in the next rise. A cart wheel could still never fit it. I pinned the date and the width on the same scrap. Ask Lark to keep both if it goes through a press.
byOutcome.bend: A cart made the longer bend in the next rise. The wind pulled the second knot on the screen loose. I wrote that on the route slip before the cart turned home. I hope the next copy keeps the knot.

byOutcome.fold: The stalls rigged their own board. A whole copy reaches them now. I left a wide margin for the trial date. There is always room for more heading. The date is harder to persuade.
byOutcome.pair: I sent a spare clip with the runner. She says a string will do better in the wet. Your next chart will meet weather before it meets its next reader. I would ask the deck crew what stays put.
byOutcome.wait: The caller tried taking the signed order down to the stalls. They could hear the directions there. A person at the ramp could not. We set the full order by the hoist while the caller walks.

byOutcome.quay: I kept the next quay turn. A guest arrived just as I reached for my coat. We had one dry bench and two stories. The new rota beside the lamp told me whose coat to reach for after mine.
byOutcome.room: The visitor who missed the quay light found the room arrow and waited by the near shelf. I moved the chair so the next person can see it from the doorway. Two steps made the difference.
byOutcome.defer: The morning keeper set out the promised chair. Our first visitor had already taken a boat. We’ve left a second date on the card. We can still keep a place without pretending everyone can come.
